questions.stem: In paediatric neurosurgery, which imaging modalities are used for investigation?
In paediatric neurosurgery, which general principles are the same as in adults?
questions.answer: Record preoperative neurological status; control ICP and BP; neuroprotection

questions.stem: Which coma scale is used in children older than 4 years in paediatric neurosurgery?

options: It causes hypocapnia, which lowers ICP
It speeds gastric emptying before induction
Respiratory depression causes hypercapnia, which raises ICP
It increases airway secretions and laryngospasm

questions.stem: In paediatric neurosurgery, when may a shoulder roll be needed for airway positioning?
options: For a child with a cleft palate
For a child with a tracheostomy
For a child with bulbar palsy

questions.stem: Which induction is preferred for a child with raised ICP and no easy IV access?

questions.answer: The head lies above the heart even when supine

questions.stem: In paediatric neurosurgery, what is hydrocephalus?
questions.answer: Abnormal CSF accumulation in the cranium

questions.stem: Name three causes of acquired hydrocephalus in children.

questions.answer: Big head, bulging fontanelle, engorged veins and sun setting eyes

questions.stem: In paediatric hydrocephalus, what does a VP shunt do?
questions.answer: Diverts CSF from the ventricle to the peritoneum via a low-pressure valved shunt

questions.stem: In non-communicating hydrocephalus, which procedure links the third ventricle to the subarachnoid space?

questions.answer: A self-sealing dome reservoir under the scalp with a ventricular catheter

questions.stem: Why is neurology reassessed regularly on the ward in children with hydrocephalus?
options: Ward staff rarely observe the child

questions.stem: What problems does raised ICP bring in children awaiting hydrocephalus surgery?
questions.answer: Vomiting, dehydration, reduced consciousness and aspiration risk

questions.stem: Which problems are common in ex-premature children having hydrocephalus surgery?
questions.answer: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia, oxygen need, difficult venous access

questions.stem: In neonates with hydrocephalus, which finding is an important sign of raised ICP?

questions.answer: If a cannula is in place or easily placed

questions.stem: In hydrocephalus, why is gas induction often the realistic choice in infants?
questions.answer: Difficult cannulation with crying harms ICP more than gas induction

questions.stem: In hydrocephalus surgery, what is the usual fentanyl dose in children?

In paediatric hydrocephalus surgery, how much blood loss is usual?
How does local anaesthetic at the surgical site help in hydrocephalus surgery?
Which children need apnoea monitoring after hydrocephalus surgery?
questions.answer: Preterm babies and those with neural tube defects

questions.stem: After hydrocephalus surgery in children, how is respiratory support stepped up?
questions.answer: Oxygen to nasal CPAP, then nasal CPAP to intubation and IPPV

questions.stem: What causes spasticity in cerebral palsy?
questions.answer: Loss of descending inhibition in the cord

questions.stem: How does intrathecal baclofen act in the spinal cord?
options: NMDA receptor antagonism in the cortex
Dopamine D2 blockade in the striatum

questions.stem: What limits oral baclofen therapy?
questions.answer: Somnolence, confusion, ataxia and urinary frequency

questions.stem: How does intrathecal baclofen compare with oral baclofen?
options: Needs higher doses with more side effects
Works only in adults with spasticity
Works at lower doses with fewer side effects
Is given as a single bolus only

questions.stem: How long is the intrathecal baclofen trial before a pump is implanted?
Where is the baclofen pump placed in the body?
options: Subcutaneous pocket in the lateral abdominal wall

questions.stem: How is an implanted baclofen pump refilled?
What infection rate is quoted for intrathecal baclofen pump complications?
Apart from infection, what are baclofen pump complications?
How have numbers needing general anaesthesia for baclofen pump insertion changed?
questions.answer: Risen markedly over the last decade

questions.stem: Which cerebral palsy issues matter for anaesthesia before baclofen pump insertion?
questions.answer: Respiratory function, reflux, impaired airway reflexes, epilepsy and medications

questions.stem: Besides usual medicines, which premedication may be given before baclofen pump surgery?
questions.answer: Antisialogogue, sedative or antacid, as indicated

questions.stem: Before baclofen pump surgery, venous access may be ____.
What guides the induction choice for baclofen pump insertion?
What airway management is usual for baclofen pump insertion?
What position is usually used for baclofen pump insertion?
What precautions are needed when positioning a child for baclofen pump surgery?
questions.answer: Pad pressure points, care with contractures, keep warm, guard against aspiration

questions.stem: What morphine dose is used for analgesia in baclofen pump surgery?

How long is a baclofen pump purged at the end of surgery?
What fluids are given after baclofen pump insertion, and until when?
How soon does spasticity usually ease after starting intrathecal baclofen?
What are the signs of intrathecal baclofen overdose?
questions.answer: Drowsiness, respiratory depression, ascending hypotonia, loss of consciousness

questions.stem: What can abrupt withdrawal of intrathecal baclofen cause, and for how long?
questions.answer: Seizures, hallucinations, disorientation, dyskinesia and itch, lasting up to 72 hours

questions.stem: What is the commonest reason for craniotomy in children?

What is the peak age range for children having craniotomy for tumour?

Apart from tumours, what are other indications for paediatric craniotomy?
questions.answer: Epilepsy, head injury, vascular lesions, craniosynostosis

questions.stem: What neurological features should be assessed before paediatric craniotomy?
questions.answer: Raised ICP, conscious level, focal signs such as cranial nerve palsies

questions.stem: What may bulbar palsy have caused before craniotomy in a child?

questions.answer: Fentanyl or remifentanil bolus with adequate depth

questions.stem: Which endotracheal tube is advised for craniotomy in children?
In paediatric craniotomy, a thicker-walled airway tube may need an internal diameter ____ than the age-based size.

questions.answer: Good operating conditions and rapid wake-up for neurological assessment

questions.stem: Paediatric craniotomy maintenance uses a volatile agent in oxygen and air or ____.

questions.answer: Lowers volatile need and gives moderate, stable hypotension

questions.answer: Pressor responses to head pins, incision, dural opening and closure

questions.stem: In paediatric craniotomy, when is deliberate hyperventilation appropriate?
options: Routinely, to keep CO2 low throughout
Only for acute rises in intracranial pressure

What invasive monitoring is recommended for major paediatric craniotomy cases?

questions.answer: Long cases, after mannitol or diuretic, expected high urine output, or major bleeding

questions.stem: What position is most paediatric craniotomy cases performed in?

questions.answer: Moderate head-up and free jugular veins

questions.stem: Why is venous kinking more likely in small children during craniotomy positioning?

questions.answer: Hyperosmolar or hypo-osmolar fluids, as they worsen cerebral oedema

questions.answer: Clinical state, urine output and serial haematocrit

questions.stem: After paediatric craniotomy, what assessment is made early, before regular HDU checks?

What oral morphine dose is used for analgesia after paediatric craniotomy?
After paediatric craniotomy, why may NSAIDs be held early?

questions.answer: IV morphine infusion, by NCA or PCA
